ca_middle_cliff.blurb: Middle Cliff is a small bolted wall in the New Directions cluster, just north of Kernville above the Kern River. Ten routes, nearly all sport with a single top-rope line, run from about 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk sitting between 5.9 and 5.11. Look for the horizontal roof systems above the pullout to spot it. The newer lines on the left side are short and well protected, while the easier routes toward the right are reputed to feel stiffer than their numbers suggest. It is a cool-season choice, best from late fall through early spring, and gets very hot in summer.
ca_middle_cliff.approach: A short way south of the pullout, a cairned trail leaves the road and climbs the hill, then bends to climbers' left to reach the base.

ca_half_day_dome.blurb: Half Day Dome is a compact crag poking out of the trees near Chilkoot Lake, at the northern end of Shuteye Ridge and a manageable drive from Fresno. Ten routes mix five sport lines, four trad lines and one aid route, with grades from 5.9 to 5.12 and most of them in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. There are a handful of moderates for warming up before moving on to the steeper 5.11 faces and arete, and a hard 5.12 for the ambitious. The area around the lake tends to be quiet.

ca_butcher_block_3.blurb: Butcher Block is a big flat-topped boulder standing in Mill Creek at Thurman Flat, in the San Bernardino Mountains near Redlands. Ten problems are described here, running from V0 to V5, with most in the V0 to V2 range and a few harder power problems around V4 and V5. Many problems are short, eight to ten feet, and use sit starts, so pads matter. The creek level changes through the year and can leave some starts underwater. The walk from the car is five minutes or less, which makes it a convenient quick session close to the road.

ca_condome_2.blurb: Condome is a granite dome in the Shaver Lake area of the western Sierra, sitting between the north end of Bald Mountain and the lake. The formation has two tiers with most of the routes on the lower one, and the climbing is mostly bolted slab. Ten routes are listed here, seven sport and three trad, from 5.8 to about 5.10, with the greatest number around 5.10. Some gear can be handy, particularly for building anchors if you carry on to the top of the lower tier. It is a quiet corner for moderate slab, and the walk from the road is short.

ca_basement_the_2.blurb: The Basement is a section of The Freaks, a bouldering zone near Silver Lake beside Highway 88 in the Carson Pass corridor. It holds ten problems on steep volcanic stone, among the hardest and most overhanging roof problems around Tahoe. Grades start near V3 and then jump into hard territory, with several problems from V7 up past V10 and a couple in the V12 range, so it is mainly for strong boulderers. The ground below the main walls is confined and dusty. Reaching it takes a hike of ten minutes or so from the trailhead to the main boulders, then a few more minutes up steep switchbacks.

ca_1_space_domes.blurb: Space Domes is a small cluster of micro domes on Lake Tahoe's South Shore, part of the Pie Shop zone and set across a gully from the Space Invaders boulder. Ten routes, six sport and four trad, offer short, challenging climbing on sharp, sun-warmed south-facing stone, which makes it a good winter objective. Grades run from 5.9 into the 5.13 range, with the majority around 5.11. Anchors are bolted. The trail climbs to the top of a dome, and you then walk around either side to reach the base of the routes.

ca_beach_boulder.blurb: Beach Boulder is a wall of problems in the Beach Area of Mount Rubidoux, the boulder-covered hill above Riverside. Ten climbs are listed, nearly all boulder problems from VB to about V2, plus one top-rope line. The stone here is finer-textured and gentler on the fingertips than most of the hill. The main wall is tall enough that a steady head and a pad or two are recommended. Reach it by walking uphill from the park on the paved access road, north toward the summit cross.
